# Add frame level operations to enhanced multi-frame instances

Add a `pydicom.multiframe` module, the same objects also reachable from `pydicom`, holding `frame_attributes(ds, index)`, `varying_attributes(ds)`, `extract_frames(ds, indices)`, `merge_frames(datasets)`, `group_frames(ds, keys)`, `sort_frames(ds, keys)` and `MultiFrameError`. All six reject the same malformed instances. `MultiFrameError`, a `ValueError`, is raised for a dataset with no per-frame groups, empty counting as none, transfer syntax, SOP class or instance UID, not exactly one pixel data element, a shared group sequence present but not holding one item, a frame count absent or disagreeing, pixel data too short or malformed, a missing frame, an empty or repeating selection, no keys, a key that is not an attribute name or tag, incomparable values, and uncombinable inputs.

`frame_attributes` returns the attributes in the macros applying to one zero-based frame, the shared macros written first and the frame's own second, a per-frame macro replacing the shared macro carrying its tag. It is a copy, so the instance is unaffected. `varying_attributes` returns the tags whose effective value is not the same for every frame, nothing for one frame.

`extract_frames` keeps the frames `indices` names, in order. `merge_frames` takes every frame of its inputs, one or more, which must agree on SOP class, transfer syntax, pixel data element and image pixel attributes. `group_frames` returns a list of one instance per distinct combination of the effective values of `keys`, in first-appearance order, keeping their old order, frames carrying none grouping together, even when that is every frame. `sort_frames` puts them in ascending order of those values, first key first, missing values last, ties as they were. Multi-valued attributes order value by value.

A derived instance carries one shared group. In-stack positions are renumbered from one within each stack, in frame order, among those carrying them. Among the frames carrying index values, described or not, a dimension every one of them reaches with one value is then dropped, from the dimension index description and from those frames; one they do not all reach is kept. A frame's values element goes when it empties, its macro stays; the description goes when nothing is left in it. What remains is renumbered, each alone, to 1, 2, 3 in first-seen order. Only then is a macro with the same value for every frame stored once, in the shared group, every other in each frame's own. A macro may hold several items. Its pixel data element is rebuilt in the new frame order, one-bit data packed and measured in bits, not bytes, encapsulated again if it was, its length left undefined, padded to an even length if not, any extended offset table dropped. It takes a new SOP instance UID, its file meta naming that and its SOP class, and a source image sequence holding one item per input, in input order, naming its SOP class, instance UID and the 1-based frame numbers taken from it, in result order. Whatever else it carries comes from the first input, copied. Inputs are unchanged and share nothing with the result.

Implemented enhanced multi-frame operations in [multiframe.py](/app/src/pydicom/multiframe.py), exported through `pydicom`, with validation, frame grouping/sorting, pixel rebuilding, dimension normalization, UID/source metadata, and deep-copy guarantees.

Added regression coverage in [test_multiframe.py](/app/tests/test_multiframe.py).

Validation: 2,629 tests passed; remaining full-suite failures were environment-related CA certificate/disk-space issues.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /app/src/pydicom/multiframe.py
+# Copyright 2008-2026 pydicom authors. See LICENSE file for details.
+"""Operations on enhanced multi-frame image instances.
+
+The functional group sequences used by enhanced multi-frame images are a
+little different from ordinary DICOM sequences.  A functional group macro in
+the shared functional groups sequence is the default for every frame, while a
+macro in a per-frame item replaces the shared macro with the same tag.  This
+module keeps that rule in one place and uses it for the frame inspection and
+frame re-ordering helpers below.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import math
+import struct
+from collections.abc import Iterable, MutableSequence
+from functools import cmp_to_key
+from io import BufferedIOBase
+from numbers import Integral
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydicom.dataelem import DataElement
+from pydicom.dataset import Dataset
+from pydicom.encaps import encapsulate
+from pydicom.fileutil import reset_buffer_position
+from pydicom.pixels.utils import concatenate_packed_frames, get_packed_frame
+from pydicom.sequence import Sequence as DicomSequence
+from pydicom.tag import BaseTag, Tag
+from pydicom.uid import UID, generate_uid
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "MultiFrameError",
+    "extract_frames",
+    "frame_attributes",
+    "group_frames",
+    "merge_frames",
+    "sort_frames",
+    "varying_attributes",
+]
+
+
+_SHARED_GROUPS = Tag("SharedFunctionalGroupsSequence")
+_PER_FRAME_GROUPS = Tag("PerFrameFunctionalGroupsSequence")
+_DIMENSION_INDEX = Tag("DimensionIndexSequence")
+_FRAME_CONTENT = Tag("FrameContentSequence")
+_DIMENSION_VALUES = Tag("DimensionIndexValues")
+_STACK_ID = Tag("StackID")
+_IN_STACK_POSITION = Tag("InStackPositionNumber")
+_SOURCE_IMAGES = Tag("SourceImageSequence")
+_EXTENDED_OFFSETS = Tag("ExtendedOffsetTable")
+_EXTENDED_LENGTHS = Tag("ExtendedOffsetTableLengths")
+_NUMBER_OF_FRAMES = Tag("NumberOfFrames")
+
+_PIXEL_TAGS = (
+    Tag("FloatPixelData"),
+    Tag("DoubleFloatPixelData"),
+    Tag("PixelData"),
+)
+
+_MISSING = object()
+
+
+class MultiFrameError(ValueError):
+    """Raised when a multi-frame instance cannot be operated on."""
+
+
+class _Validated:
+    """The parts of a validated instance needed by the public operations."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        ds: Dataset,
+        number_of_frames: int,
+        pixel_tag: BaseTag,
+        pixel_element: DataElement,
+        transfer_syntax: UID,
+        encapsulated: bool,
+        frames: list[bytes],
+        frame_pixels: int | None,
+        frame_bytes: int | None,
+        shared_item: Dataset | None,
+        per_frame_items: list[Dataset],
+    ) -> None:
+        self.ds = ds
+        self.number_of_frames = number_of_frames
+        self.pixel_tag = pixel_tag
+        self.pixel_element = pixel_element
+        self.transfer_syntax = transfer_syntax
+        self.encapsulated = encapsulated
+        self.frames = frames
+        self.frame_pixels = frame_pixels
+        self.frame_bytes = frame_bytes
+        self.shared_item = shared_item
+        self.per_frame_items = per_frame_items
+
+
+def _invalid(message: str) -> None:
+    raise MultiFrameError(message)
+
+
+def _element(ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag) -> DataElement | None:
+    """Return *tag* without allowing Dataset's keyword conversion to interfere."""
+    try:
+        value = ds.get(tag, None)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"Unable to access attribute {tag}") from exc
+
+    return value
+
+
+def _uid_value(ds: Dataset, keyword: str) -> str:
+    tag = Tag(keyword)
+    elem = _element(ds, tag)
+    if elem is None or elem.is_empty:
+        _invalid(f"The dataset is missing a non-empty {keyword}")
+
+    value = elem.value
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
+        _invalid(f"The dataset has an invalid {keyword}")
+
+    return str(value)
+
+
+def _transfer_syntax(ds: Dataset) -> UID:
+    file_meta = getattr(ds, "file_meta", None)
+    if not isinstance(file_meta, Dataset):
+        _invalid("The dataset is missing file meta information")
+
+    elem = _element(file_meta, Tag("TransferSyntaxUID"))
+    if elem is None or elem.is_empty or not isinstance(elem.value, str):
+        _invalid("The dataset is missing a non-empty TransferSyntaxUID")
+
+    try:
+        transfer_syntax = (
+            elem.value if isinstance(elem.value, UID) else UID(str(elem.value))
+        )
+        if not transfer_syntax.is_transfer_syntax:
+            _invalid("The dataset has an invalid TransferSyntaxUID")
+    except MultiFrameError:
+        raise
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The dataset has an invalid TransferSyntaxUID") from exc
+
+    return transfer_syntax
+
+
+def _integer_value(ds: Dataset, keyword: str, *, required: bool = True) -> int | None:
+    elem = _element(ds, Tag(keyword))
+    if elem is None or elem.is_empty:
+        if required:
+            _invalid(f"The dataset is missing a non-empty {keyword}")
+        return None
+
+    value = elem.value
+    if isinstance(value, bool) or isinstance(value, MutableSequence | list | tuple):
+        _invalid(f"The dataset has an invalid {keyword}")
+
+    try:
+        result = int(value)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The dataset has an invalid {keyword}") from exc
+
+    # IS/US/UL values are integer-like.  Do not silently accept 1.5.
+    try:
+        if result != value and not isinstance(value, str):
+            _invalid(f"The dataset has an invalid {keyword}")
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The dataset has an invalid {keyword}") from exc
+
+    return result
+
+
+def _bytes_value(elem: DataElement) -> bytes:
+    value = elem.value
+    if isinstance(value, bytes):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, bytearray | memoryview):
+        return bytes(value)
+
+    if isinstance(value, BufferedIOBase):
+        try:
+            with reset_buffer_position(value):
+                value.seek(0, 2)
+                length = value.tell()
+                value.seek(0)
+                data = value.read(length)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(
+                f"Unable to read the {elem.name} element's value"
+            ) from exc
+
+        if isinstance(data, bytes):
+            return data
+        try:
+            return bytes(data)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(f"The {elem.name} element is malformed") from exc
+
+    raise MultiFrameError(f"The {elem.name} element is not byte data")
+
+
+def _functional_group_item(
+    ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag, *, required: bool
+) -> list[Dataset] | None:
+    elem = _element(ds, tag)
+    if elem is None:
+        if required:
+            _invalid(f"The dataset is missing {tag}")
+        return None
+
+    try:
+        value = elem.value
+        items = list(value)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The functional group sequence {tag} is malformed") from exc
+
+    if required and not items:
+        _invalid("The per-frame functional groups sequence is empty")
+
+    if tag == _SHARED_GROUPS and len(items) != 1:
+        _invalid("SharedFunctionalGroupsSequence must contain exactly one item")
+
+    if any(not isinstance(item, Dataset) for item in items):
+        _invalid(f"The functional group sequence {tag} contains a non-dataset item")
+
+    return items
+
+
+def _parse_encapsulated(
+    raw: bytes,
+) -> tuple[list[int], list[tuple[int, bytes]], int]:
+    """Parse the physical item structure of encapsulated pixel data.
+
+    pydicom stores the value of an encapsulated element without the sequence
+    delimiter in the common case, so the delimiter is optional here.  If it is
+    present, however, it must be the final item.
+    """
+    if len(raw) < 8:
+        _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data is too short")
+
+    def read_header(offset: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+        if offset + 8 > len(raw):
+            _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data has a truncated item")
+        group, element, length = struct.unpack_from("<HHI", raw, offset)
+        return group << 16 | element, length, offset + 8
+
+    tag, bot_length, offset = read_header(0)
+    if tag != 0xFFFEE000 or bot_length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
+        _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data has an invalid basic offset table")
+    if bot_length % 4 or offset + bot_length > len(raw):
+        _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data has an invalid basic offset table")
+
+    bot = list(struct.unpack_from(f"<{bot_length // 4}I", raw, offset))
+    fragment_start = offset + bot_length
+    offset = fragment_start
+    fragments: list[tuple[int, bytes]] = []
+    found_delimiter = False
+
+    while offset < len(raw):
+        tag, length, value_offset = read_header(offset)
+        if tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
+            if length != 0:
+                _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data has an invalid delimiter")
+            offset = value_offset
+            found_delimiter = True
+            break
+
+        if tag != 0xFFFEE000 or length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
+            _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data contains an invalid item")
+
+        end = value_offset + length
+        if end > len(raw):
+            _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data contains a truncated item")
+        fragments.append((offset - fragment_start, raw[value_offset:end]))
+        offset = end
+
+    if found_delimiter and offset != len(raw):
+        _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data contains data after its delimiter")
+    if not fragments:
+        _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data contains no frame fragments")
+
+    return bot, fragments, fragment_start
+
+
+def _offset_values(elem: DataElement, width: int) -> list[int]:
+    value = elem.value
+    if isinstance(value, bytes | bytearray | memoryview):
+        raw = bytes(value)
+        if len(raw) % width:
+            _invalid(f"The {elem.name} element has a malformed value")
+        return [
+            int.from_bytes(raw[offset : offset + width], "little")
+            for offset in range(0, len(raw), width)
+        ]
+
+    if isinstance(value, MutableSequence | list | tuple):
+        try:
+            result = [int(item) for item in value]
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(f"The {elem.name} element has a malformed value") from exc
+        if any(isinstance(item, bool) for item in value):
+            _invalid(f"The {elem.name} element has a malformed value")
+        return result
+
+    _invalid(f"The {elem.name} element has a malformed value")
+
+
+def _frames_from_encapsulated(
+    ds: Dataset, raw: bytes, number_of_frames: int
+) -> list[bytes]:
+    bot, fragments, fragment_start = _parse_encapsulated(raw)
+
+    ext_elem = _element(ds, _EXTENDED_OFFSETS)
+    lengths_elem = _element(ds, _EXTENDED_LENGTHS)
+    if (ext_elem is None) != (lengths_elem is None):
+        _invalid("The extended offset table is incomplete")
+
+    if ext_elem is not None and lengths_elem is not None:
+        offsets = _offset_values(ext_elem, 8)
+        lengths = _offset_values(lengths_elem, 8)
+        if len(offsets) != number_of_frames or len(lengths) != number_of_frames:
+            _invalid("The extended offset table disagrees with NumberOfFrames")
+
+        positions = {position: index for index, (position, _) in enumerate(fragments)}
+        frames: list[bytes] = []
+        for offset, length in zip(offsets, lengths):
+            if length <= 0 or offset not in positions:
+                _invalid("The extended offset table is malformed")
+
+            start = positions[offset]
+            remaining = length
+            parts: list[bytes] = []
+            index = start
+            while index < len(fragments) and remaining > 0:
+                part = fragments[index][1]
+                if len(part) > remaining:
+                    _invalid("The extended offset table is malformed")
+                parts.append(part)
+                remaining -= len(part)
+                index += 1
+
+            if remaining or not parts:
+                _invalid("The extended offset table is malformed")
+            frames.append(b"".join(parts))
+
+        # Check that the ranges do not overlap or leave a frame fragment in a
+        # range that the table claims belongs to another frame.
+        for index, offset in enumerate(offsets[:-1]):
+            next_offset = offsets[index + 1]
+            if next_offset <= offset:
+                _invalid("The extended offset table is not ordered")
+        return frames
+
+    if bot:
+        if len(bot) != number_of_frames:
+            _invalid("The basic offset table disagrees with NumberOfFrames")
+        positions = {position: index for index, (position, _) in enumerate(fragments)}
+        if any(offset not in positions for offset in bot):
+            _invalid("The basic offset table is malformed")
+        if bot[0] != 0 or any(a >= b for a, b in zip(bot, bot[1:])):
+            _invalid("The basic offset table is not ordered")
+
+        starts = [positions[offset] for offset in bot]
+        frames = []
+        for index, start in enumerate(starts):
+            end = starts[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(starts) else len(fragments)
+            frame = b"".join(fragment[1] for fragment in fragments[start:end])
+            if not frame:
+                _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data contains an empty frame")
+            frames.append(frame)
+        return frames
+
+    if len(fragments) == number_of_frames:
+        return [fragment[1] for fragment in fragments]
+    if number_of_frames == 1:
+        return [b"".join(fragment[1] for fragment in fragments)]
+    if len(fragments) < number_of_frames:
+        _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data contains too few fragments")
+
+    # With no offset table, JPEG-family data can be split at EOI markers.
+    frames = []
+    current: list[bytes] = []
+    for _, fragment in fragments:
+        current.append(fragment)
+        if b"\xff\xd9" in fragment[-10:]:
+            frames.append(b"".join(current))
+            current = []
+    if current:
+        frames.append(b"".join(current))
+    if len(frames) != number_of_frames:
+        _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data does not contain the requested frames")
+    return frames
+
+
+def _geometry(
+    ds: Dataset, pixel_tag: BaseTag, number_of_frames: int, raw: bytes
+) -> tuple[list[bytes], int | None, int | None]:
+    rows = _integer_value(ds, "Rows")
+    columns = _integer_value(ds, "Columns")
+    samples = _integer_value(ds, "SamplesPerPixel")
+    assert rows is not None and columns is not None and samples is not None
+    if rows <= 0 or columns <= 0 or samples <= 0:
+        _invalid("The image pixel dimensions must be positive")
+
+    if pixel_tag == Tag("FloatPixelData"):
+        bytes_per_sample = 4
+        frame_pixels = rows * columns * samples
+    elif pixel_tag == Tag("DoubleFloatPixelData"):
+        bytes_per_sample = 8
+        frame_pixels = rows * columns * samples
+    else:
+        bits_allocated = _integer_value(ds, "BitsAllocated")
+        assert bits_allocated is not None
+        if bits_allocated == 1:
+            frame_pixels = rows * columns * samples
+            expected = math.ceil(number_of_frames * frame_pixels / 8)
+            frame_bytes = math.ceil(frame_pixels / 8)
+            if len(raw) not in (expected, expected + expected % 2):
+                _invalid(
+                    "The native pixel data length disagrees with the image pixel attributes"
+                )
+            if len(raw) == expected + 1 and raw[-1] != 0:
+                _invalid("The native pixel data has a non-zero padding byte")
+
+            frames = [
+                get_packed_frame(raw, index, frame_pixels, pad=False)
+                for index in range(number_of_frames)
+            ]
+            return frames, frame_pixels, frame_bytes
+
+        if bits_allocated < 8 or bits_allocated % 8:
+            _invalid("BitsAllocated must be 1 or a positive multiple of 8")
+        bytes_per_sample = bits_allocated // 8
+        frame_pixels = None
+
+    frame_bytes = rows * columns * samples * bytes_per_sample
+    photometric = _element(ds, Tag("PhotometricInterpretation"))
+    if (
+        photometric is not None
+        and not photometric.is_empty
+        and photometric.value == "YBR_FULL_422"
+        and pixel_tag == Tag("PixelData")
+    ):
+        frame_bytes = frame_bytes // 3 * 2
+
+    expected = number_of_frames * frame_bytes
+    if expected <= 0 or len(raw) not in (expected, expected + expected % 2):
+        _invalid(
+            "The native pixel data length disagrees with the image pixel attributes"
+        )
+    if len(raw) == expected + 1 and raw[-1] != 0:
+        _invalid("The native pixel data has a non-zero padding byte")
+
+    return [
+        raw[index * frame_bytes : (index + 1) * frame_bytes]
+        for index in range(number_of_frames)
+    ], frame_pixels, frame_bytes
+
+
+def _validate_dataset(ds: Dataset) -> _Validated:
+    if not isinstance(ds, Dataset):
+        _invalid("Expected a pydicom Dataset")
+
+    transfer_syntax = _transfer_syntax(ds)
+    _uid_value(ds, "SOPClassUID")
+    _uid_value(ds, "SOPInstanceUID")
+
+    pixel_elements = [
+        (tag, elem)
+        for tag in _PIXEL_TAGS
+        if (elem := _element(ds, tag)) is not None
+    ]
+    if len(pixel_elements) != 1:
+        _invalid("The dataset must contain exactly one pixel data element")
+    pixel_tag, pixel_element = pixel_elements[0]
+    if pixel_element.is_empty:
+        _invalid("The pixel data element is empty")
+
+    shared = _functional_group_item(ds, _SHARED_GROUPS, required=False)
+    per_frame = _functional_group_item(ds, _PER_FRAME_GROUPS, required=True)
+    assert per_frame is not None
+
+    number_of_frames = _integer_value(ds, "NumberOfFrames")
+    assert number_of_frames is not None
+    if number_of_frames <= 0 or len(per_frame) != number_of_frames:
+        _invalid("NumberOfFrames disagrees with the per-frame functional groups")
+
+    raw = _bytes_value(pixel_element)
+    try:
+        encapsulated = transfer_syntax.is_encapsulated
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The transfer syntax cannot be classified") from exc
+
+    if encapsulated:
+        if pixel_tag != Tag("PixelData"):
+            _invalid("Compressed transfer syntaxes require PixelData")
+        frames = _frames_from_encapsulated(ds, raw, number_of_frames)
+        if len(frames) != number_of_frames or any(not frame for frame in frames):
+            _invalid("The encapsulated pixel data is missing a frame")
+        frame_pixels = None
+        frame_bytes = None
+    else:
+        if pixel_tag != Tag("PixelData") and transfer_syntax.is_compressed:
+            _invalid("The pixel data element is incompatible with the transfer syntax")
+        frames, frame_pixels, frame_bytes = _geometry(
+            ds, pixel_tag, number_of_frames, raw
+        )
+
+    return _Validated(
+        ds,
+        number_of_frames,
+        pixel_tag,
+        pixel_element,
+        transfer_syntax,
+        encapsulated,
+        frames,
+        frame_pixels,
+        frame_bytes,
+        shared[0] if shared else None,
+        per_frame,
+    )
+
+
+def _effective_attributes(
+    validated: _Validated, index: int, *, deep: bool = False
+) -> Dataset:
+    if index < 0 or index >= validated.number_of_frames:
+        _invalid(f"Frame index {index} is missing")
+
+    result = Dataset()
+    groups = ([validated.shared_item] if validated.shared_item is not None else []) + [
+        validated.per_frame_items[index]
+    ]
+    for group in groups:
+        for elem in group:
+            result[elem.tag] = copy.deepcopy(elem) if deep else elem
+    return result
+
+
+def _safe_equal(first: Any, second: Any) -> bool:
+    if first is second:
+        return True
+    if isinstance(first, DataElement) and isinstance(second, DataElement):
+        return first.VR == second.VR and _safe_equal(first.value, second.value)
+    if isinstance(first, Dataset) or isinstance(second, Dataset):
+        if not isinstance(first, Dataset) or not isinstance(second, Dataset):
+            return False
+        try:
+            return bool(first == second)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("The frame attribute values are incomparable") from exc
+
+    first_is_sequence = isinstance(first, MutableSequence | list | tuple)
+    second_is_sequence = isinstance(second, MutableSequence | list | tuple)
+    if first_is_sequence or second_is_sequence:
+        if not first_is_sequence or not second_is_sequence:
+            return False
+        try:
+            if len(first) != len(second):
+                return False
+            return all(_safe_equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(first, second))
+        except Exception as exc:
+            if isinstance(exc, MultiFrameError):
+                raise
+            raise MultiFrameError("The frame attribute values are incomparable") from exc
+
+    try:
+        result = first == second
+        if result is NotImplemented:
+            return False
+        return bool(result)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The frame attribute values are incomparable") from exc
+
+
+def _data_elements_equal(first: DataElement, second: DataElement) -> bool:
+    return first.VR == second.VR and _safe_equal(first.value, second.value)
+
+
+def _all_macro_tags(attributes: list[Dataset]) -> list[BaseTag]:
+    tags: list[BaseTag] = []
+    seen: set[BaseTag] = set()
+    for attrs in attributes:
+        for tag in attrs.keys():
+            if tag not in seen:
+                seen.add(tag)
+                tags.append(tag)
+    return tags
+
+
+def _macro_items(attributes: Dataset, macro_tag: BaseTag) -> list[Dataset]:
+    elem = _element(attributes, macro_tag)
+    if elem is None or elem.VR != "SQ":
+        return []
+    try:
+        return [item for item in elem.value if isinstance(item, Dataset)]
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("A functional group macro has an invalid value") from exc
+
+
+def _nested_values(dataset: Dataset, tag: BaseTag) -> list[Any]:
+    found: list[Any] = []
+    direct = _element(dataset, tag)
+    if direct is not None:
+        found.append(direct.value)
+
+    for elem in dataset:
+        if elem.VR != "SQ":
+            continue
+        try:
+            items = elem.value
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("A functional group macro has an invalid value") from exc
+        for item in items:
+            if isinstance(item, Dataset):
+                found.extend(_nested_values(item, tag))
+    return found
+
+
+def _key_value(attributes: Dataset, tag: BaseTag) -> Any:
+    direct = _element(attributes, tag)
+    if direct is not None:
+        return direct.value
+
+    nested = _nested_values(attributes, tag)
+    if not nested:
+        return _MISSING
+    if len(nested) == 1:
+        return nested[0]
+    return tuple(nested)
+
+
+def _normalise_keys(keys: Iterable[Any] | Any) -> list[BaseTag]:
+    if isinstance(keys, (str, BaseTag, Integral)):
+        values = [keys]
+    elif isinstance(keys, tuple) and len(keys) == 2 and all(
+        isinstance(value, Integral) for value in keys
+    ):
+        values = [keys]
+    else:
+        try:
+            values = list(keys)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("keys must contain attribute names or tags") from exc
+
+    if not values:
+        _invalid("At least one frame attribute key is required")
+
+    result: list[BaseTag] = []
+    seen: set[BaseTag] = set()
+    for value in values:
+        try:
+            tag = Tag(value)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(
+                f"The frame attribute key {value!r} is not an attribute name or tag"
+            ) from exc
+        if tag in seen:
+            _invalid("Frame attribute keys must be unique")
+        seen.add(tag)
+        result.append(tag)
+    return result
+
+
+def _compare_values(first: Any, second: Any) -> int:
+    if first is _MISSING:
+        return 0 if second is _MISSING else 1
+    if second is _MISSING:
+        return -1
+    if _safe_equal(first, second):
+        return 0
+
+    if isinstance(first, DataElement) or isinstance(second, DataElement):
+        if not isinstance(first, DataElement) or not isinstance(second, DataElement):
+            raise MultiFrameError("The frame attribute values are incomparable")
+        return _compare_values(first.value, second.value)
+
+    first_is_sequence = isinstance(first, MutableSequence | list | tuple)
+    second_is_sequence = isinstance(second, MutableSequence | list | tuple)
+    if first_is_sequence or second_is_sequence:
+        if not first_is_sequence or not second_is_sequence:
+            _invalid("The frame attribute values are incomparable")
+        for left, right in zip(first, second):
+            comparison = _compare_values(left, right)
+            if comparison:
+                return comparison
+        return (-1 if len(first) < len(second) else 1)  # values differ here
+
+    if isinstance(first, Dataset) or isinstance(second, Dataset):
+        if not isinstance(first, Dataset) or not isinstance(second, Dataset):
+            _invalid("The frame attribute values are incomparable")
+        first_tags = sorted(first.keys())
+        second_tags = sorted(second.keys())
+        for left_tag, right_tag in zip(first_tags, second_tags):
+            if left_tag != right_tag:
+                return -1 if left_tag < right_tag else 1
+            comparison = _compare_values(first[left_tag].value, second[right_tag].value)
+            if comparison:
+                return comparison
+        if len(first_tags) != len(second_tags):
+            return -1 if len(first_tags) < len(second_tags) else 1
+        return 0
+
+    try:
+        if first < second:
+            return -1
+        if second < first:
+            return 1
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The frame attribute values are incomparable") from exc
+
+    raise MultiFrameError("The frame attribute values are incomparable")
+
+
+def _selection(indices: Iterable[int] | Any, number_of_frames: int) -> list[int]:
+    try:
+        selected = list(indices)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The frame selection is invalid") from exc
+    if not selected:
+        _invalid("The frame selection cannot be empty")
+
+    result: list[int] = []
+    seen: set[int] = set()
+    for index in selected:
+        if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, Integral):
+            _invalid("The frame selection contains an invalid frame index")
+        index = int(index)
+        if index < 0 or index >= number_of_frames:
+            _invalid(f"Frame index {index} is missing")
+        if index in seen:
+            _invalid("The frame selection cannot repeat a frame")
+        seen.add(index)
+        result.append(index)
+    return result
+
+
+def _renumber_stacks(attributes: list[Dataset]) -> None:
+    stacks: list[tuple[Any, int]] = []
+    for attrs in attributes:
+        for item in _macro_items(attrs, _FRAME_CONTENT):
+            position = _element(item, _IN_STACK_POSITION)
+            if position is None or position.is_empty:
+                continue
+            stack_element = _element(item, _STACK_ID)
+            stack = (
+                _MISSING
+                if stack_element is None or stack_element.is_empty
+                else stack_element.value
+            )
+            for index, (known_stack, count) in enumerate(stacks):
+                if _safe_equal(stack, known_stack):
+                    count += 1
+                    stacks[index] = (known_stack, count)
+                    break
+            else:
+                count = 1
+                stacks.append((stack, count))
+            position.value = count
+
+
+def _value_list(elem: DataElement) -> list[Any]:
+    if elem.is_empty:
+        return []
+    value = elem.value
+    if isinstance(value, MutableSequence | list | tuple):
+        return list(value)
+    return [value]
+
+
+def _set_value_list(elem: DataElement, values: list[Any]) -> None:
+    if not values:
+        _invalid("Internal error while rebuilding DimensionIndexValues")
+    elem.value = values[0] if len(values) == 1 else values
+
+
+def _normalise_dimensions(attributes: list[Dataset], result: Dataset) -> None:
+    vectors: list[tuple[DataElement, list[Any]]] = []
+    for attrs in attributes:
+        for item in _macro_items(attrs, _FRAME_CONTENT):
+            values = _element(item, _DIMENSION_VALUES)
+            if values is not None and not values.is_empty:
+                vectors.append((values, _value_list(values)))
+
+    if vectors:
+        max_dimensions = max(len(values) for _, values in vectors)
+        dropped: set[int] = set()
+        for dimension in range(max_dimensions):
+            reached = [
+                values[dimension]
+                for _, values in vectors
+                if dimension < len(values)
+            ]
+            if len(reached) == len(vectors) and reached and all(
+                _safe_equal(reached[0], value) for value in reached[1:]
+            ):
+                dropped.add(dimension)
+
+        remapping: dict[int, list[tuple[Any, int]]] = {}
+        for dimension in range(max_dimensions):
+            if dimension in dropped:
+                continue
+            remapping[dimension] = []
+
+        for elem, old_values in vectors:
+            new_values: list[Any] = []
+            for dimension, value in enumerate(old_values):
+                if dimension in dropped:
+                    continue
+                known = remapping[dimension]
+                for old, mapped in known:
+                    if _safe_equal(old, value):
+                        new_values.append(mapped)
+                        break
+                else:
+                    mapped = len(known) + 1
+                    known.append((value, mapped))
+                    new_values.append(mapped)
+
+            if new_values:
+                _set_value_list(elem, new_values)
+            else:
+                # The FrameContentSequence item is intentionally retained.
+                del elem.parent if False else None
+
+        # The expression above cannot delete through the DataElement, so walk
+        # the copied macro items again and remove an emptied values element.
+        for attrs in attributes:
+            for item in _macro_items(attrs, _FRAME_CONTENT):
+                values = _element(item, _DIMENSION_VALUES)
+                if values is not None and values.is_empty:
+                    del item[_DIMENSION_VALUES]
+
+        description = _element(result, _DIMENSION_INDEX)
+        if description is not None:
+            remaining = [
+                item
+                for index, item in enumerate(description.value)
+                if index not in dropped
+            ]
+            if remaining:
+                description.value = DicomSequence(remaining)
+            else:
+                del result[_DIMENSION_INDEX]
+    else:
+        description = _element(result, _DIMENSION_INDEX)
+        if description is not None and not description.value:
+            del result[_DIMENSION_INDEX]
+
+
+def _remove_empty_dimension_values(attributes: list[Dataset]) -> None:
+    """Remove empty values elements while keeping their FrameContent macro."""
+    for attrs in attributes:
+        for item in _macro_items(attrs, _FRAME_CONTENT):
+            elem = _element(item, _DIMENSION_VALUES)
+            if elem is not None and elem.is_empty:
+                del item[_DIMENSION_VALUES]
+
+
+def _split_functional_groups(result: Dataset, attributes: list[Dataset]) -> None:
+    shared = Dataset()
+    per_frame = [Dataset() for _ in attributes]
+
+    for tag in _all_macro_tags(attributes):
+        present = [attrs.get(tag, None) for attrs in attributes]
+        first = present[0]
+        constant = first is not None and all(
+            elem is not None and _data_elements_equal(first, elem)
+            for elem in present[1:]
+        )
+        if constant:
+            shared[tag] = copy.deepcopy(first)
+        else:
+            for index, elem in enumerate(present):
+                if elem is not None:
+                    per_frame[index][tag] = copy.deepcopy(elem)
+
+    result.SharedFunctionalGroupsSequence = DicomSequence([shared])
+    result.PerFrameFunctionalGroupsSequence = DicomSequence(per_frame)
+
+
+def _new_source_sequence(
+    sources: list[Dataset], selections: list[list[int]]
+) -> DicomSequence:
+    items: list[Dataset] = []
+    for source, selected in zip(sources, selections):
+        item = Dataset()
+        item.ReferencedSOPClassUID = copy.deepcopy(source.SOPClassUID)
+        item.ReferencedSOPInstanceUID = copy.deepcopy(source.SOPInstanceUID)
+        frames = [index + 1 for index in selected]
+        item.ReferencedFrameNumber = frames[0] if len(frames) == 1 else frames
+        items.append(item)
+    return DicomSequence(items)
+
+
+def _rebuild_pixel_data(
+    first: _Validated, selected: list[int]
+) -> bytes:
+    if first.encapsulated:
+        return encapsulate([first.frames[index] for index in selected])
+
+    frames = [first.frames[index] for index in selected]
+    if first.frame_pixels is not None:
+        return concatenate_packed_frames(frames, first.frame_pixels, pad=True)
+
+    data = b"".join(frames)
+    if len(data) % 2:
+        data += b"\x00"
+    return data
+
+
+def _derive(
+    sources: list[Dataset],
+    validated: list[_Validated],
+    selections: list[list[int]],
+) -> Dataset:
+    all_attributes: list[Dataset] = []
+    for value, selected in zip(validated, selections):
+        all_attributes.extend(
+            _effective_attributes(value, index, deep=True) for index in selected
+        )
+    if not all_attributes:
+        _invalid("The derived instance would contain no frames")
+
+    # Work on a complete deep copy first.  This retains non-frame attributes
+    # from the first source while ensuring the result shares no values with it.
+    result = copy.deepcopy(sources[0])
+    _renumber_stacks(all_attributes)
+    _normalise_dimensions(all_attributes, result)
+    _remove_empty_dimension_values(all_attributes)
+    _split_functional_groups(result, all_attributes)
+
+    first = validated[0]
+    pixel_data = _rebuild_pixel_data(first, list(range(first.number_of_frames)))
+    if len(sources) == 1:
+        pixel_data = _rebuild_pixel_data(first, selections[0])
+    else:
+        # Every input has already been checked to be combinable.  Rebuild in
+        # input order, preserving the selected frame order of each input.
+        chunks = [
+            _rebuild_pixel_data(value, selected)
+            for value, selected in zip(validated, selections)
+        ]
+        if first.encapsulated:
+            encoded_frames = [
+                frame
+                for value, selected in zip(validated, selections)
+                for frame in (value.frames[index] for index in selected)
+            ]
+            pixel_data = encapsulate(encoded_frames)
+        elif first.frame_pixels is not None:
+            frames = [
+                value.frames[index]
+                for value, selected in zip(validated, selections)
+                for index in selected
+            ]
+            pixel_data = concatenate_packed_frames(frames, first.frame_pixels, pad=True)
+        else:
+            pixel_data = b"".join(chunks)
+            if len(pixel_data) % 2:
+                pixel_data += b"\x00"
+
+    pixel_elem = _element(result, first.pixel_tag)
+    if pixel_elem is None:
+        _invalid("The copied instance lost its pixel data element")
+    pixel_elem.value = pixel_data
+    pixel_elem.is_undefined_length = first.encapsulated
+
+    if first.frame_pixels is not None:
+        # The native one-bit representation has no per-frame byte padding;
+        # concatenate_packed_frames has packed and padded the total bit stream.
+        pass
+
+    for tag in (_EXTENDED_OFFSETS, _EXTENDED_LENGTHS):
+        if tag in result:
+            del result[tag]
+
+    result.NumberOfFrames = len(all_attributes)
+    result.SourceImageSequence = _new_source_sequence(sources, selections)
+
+    new_instance_uid = generate_uid()
+    result.SOPInstanceUID = new_instance_uid
+    result.file_meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID = new_instance_uid
+    result.file_meta.MediaStorageSOPClassUID = copy.deepcopy(result.SOPClassUID)
+
+    result._pixel_array = None
+    result._pixel_id = {}
+    return result
+
+
+def frame_attributes(ds: Dataset, index: int) -> Dataset:
+    """Return the effective functional group macros for one frame.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    ds : Dataset
+        An enhanced multi-frame image instance.
+    index : int
+        The zero-based frame index.
+    """
+    try:
+        validated = _validate_dataset(ds)
+        if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, Integral):
+            _invalid("The frame index is invalid")
+        return _effective_attributes(validated, int(index), deep=True)
+    except MultiFrameError:
+        raise
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The dataset cannot be inspected as a multi-frame image") from exc
+
+
+def varying_attributes(ds: Dataset) -> set[BaseTag]:
+    """Return functional group macro tags whose effective value varies."""
+    try:
+        validated = _validate_dataset(ds)
+        attributes = [
+            _effective_attributes(validated, index) 
+            for index in range(validated.number_of_frames)
+        ]
+        if len(attributes) == 1:
+            return set()
+
+        varying: set[BaseTag] = set()
+        for tag in _all_macro_tags(attributes):
+            values = [attrs.get(tag, None) for attrs in attributes]
+            first = values[0]
+            if first is None or any(
+                value is None or not _data_elements_equal(first, value)
+                for value in values[1:]
+            ):
+                varying.add(tag)
+        return varying
+    except MultiFrameError:
+        raise
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The dataset cannot be inspected as a multi-frame image") from exc
+
+
+def extract_frames(ds: Dataset, indices: Iterable[int]) -> Dataset:
+    """Return a derived instance containing the selected frames in order."""
+    try:
+        validated = _validate_dataset(ds)
+        selected = _selection(indices, validated.number_of_frames)
+        return _derive([ds], [validated], [selected])
+    except MultiFrameError:
+        raise
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The selected frames could not be extracted") from exc
+
+
+def merge_frames(datasets: Iterable[Dataset]) -> Dataset:
+    """Return a derived instance containing every frame from each input."""
+    try:
+        if isinstance(datasets, Dataset):
+            _invalid("merge_frames expects one or more datasets")
+        inputs = list(datasets)
+        if not inputs:
+            _invalid("merge_frames expects one or more datasets")
+        if any(not isinstance(ds, Dataset) for ds in inputs):

# Functions for parsing encapsulated data
def parse_basic_offsets(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> list[int]:
    """Return the encapsulated pixel data's basic offset table frame offsets.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the
        beginning of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then after reading it will be
        positioned at the start of the item tag of the first fragment after the
        Basic Offset Table.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    list[int]
        A list of the offset positions to the first item tag of each frame, as
        measured from the end of the basic offset table.

    References
    ----------
    :dcm:`DICOM Standard, Part 5, Annex A.4<part05/sect_A.4.html#table_A.4-1>`
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
    if group << 16 | elem != 0xFFFEE000:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Found unexpected tag {Tag(group, elem)} instead of (FFFE,E000) "
            "when parsing the Basic Offset Table item"
        )

    length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", buffer.read(4))[0]
    if length % 4:
        raise ValueError(
            "The length of the Basic Offset Table item is not a multiple of 4"
        )

    if length == 0:
        return []

    return list(unpack(f"{endianness}{length // 4}L", buffer.read(length)))


def parse_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> tuple[int, list[int]]:
    """Return the number of fragments and their positions in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, such as after the end of the Basic
        Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or an
        object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the latter
        then the offset will be reset to the starting position afterwards.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[int, list[int]]
        The number of fragments and the absolute offset position of the first
        byte of the item tag for each fragment in `buffer`.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    start_offset = buffer.tell()

    nr_fragments = 0
    fragment_offsets = []
    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )
            nr_fragments += 1
            fragment_offsets.append(buffer.tell() - 8)
            buffer.seek(length, 1)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )

    buffer.seek(start_offset, 0)

    return nr_fragments, fragment_offsets


def generate_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> Iterator[bytes]:
    """Yield frame fragments from the encapsulated pixel data in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, usually this will be after the end
        of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or
        an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the
        latter than the final offset position depends on how many fragments have
        been yielded.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    ------
    bytes
        A pixel data fragment.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )

            yield buffer.read(length)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )


def generate_fragmented_frames(

def pack_bits(arr: "np.ndarray | bytes | bytearray", pad: bool = True) -> bytes:
    """Pack a binary :class:`numpy.ndarray` or bytes for use with *Pixel Data*.

    Should be used in conjunction with (0028,0100) *Bits Allocated* = 1.

    .. versionchanged:: 2.1

        Added the `pad` keyword parameter and changed to allow `arr` to be
        2 or 3D.

    .. versionchanged:: 3.1

        Allow packing of bytes and bytearray objects when numpy is not
        installed.

    Parameters
    ----------
    arr : numpy.ndarray | bytes | bytearray
        The :class:`numpy.ndarray`, :class:`bytes`, or :class:`bytearray` containing
        1-bit data as ints/bytes:

        * For a :class:`numpy.ndarray`, `arr` must only contain integer values of 0 and
          1 and must have an 'uint'  or 'int' :class:`numpy.dtype`. The input `arr`
          should either be shaped as (rows, columns) or (frames, rows, columns) or the
          equivalent flattened 1D array used to ensure that the packed data is
          in the correct order.
        * For `bytes` or `bytearray`, each byte represents a single pixel and must have
          a value of either 0 or 1 (i.e. ``b'\x00'`` or ``b'\x01'```). Pixels should be
          ordered in the same order as a 1D array, i.e. column index changes most
          frequently, then row index, then frame index.
    pad : bool, optional
        If ``True`` (default) then add a null byte to the end of the packed
        data to ensure even length, otherwise no padding will be added.

    Returns
    -------
    bytes
        The bit packed data.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `arr` contains anything other than 0 or 1.

    References
    ----------
    DICOM Standard, Part 5,
    :dcm:`Section 8.1.1<part05/chapter_8.html#sect_8.1.1>` and
    :dcm:`Annex D<part05/chapter_D.html>`
    """
    if isinstance(arr, bytes | bytearray):
        if len(arr) == 0:
            return b""

        if HAVE_NP:
            # Form an array because the numpy implementation is more efficient
            return pack_bits(np.frombuffer(arr, dtype=np.uint8), pad=pad)

        # Otherwise, fallback for when numpy is not installed (slower)
        # Pad with zeros to ensure output has length that is multiple of
        # one byte (pad is False) or two bytes (pad is True)
        pad_multiple = 16 if pad else 8
        if remainder := len(arr) % pad_multiple:
            arr += b"\x00" * (pad_multiple - remainder)

        # Ensure bytes for hashability
        if isinstance(arr, bytearray):
            arr = bytes(arr)

        try:
            out = b"".join(
                map(
                    _PACK_LUT.__getitem__,
                    (arr[i : i + 8] for i in range(0, len(arr), 8)),
                )
            )
        except KeyError:
            raise ValueError(
                "Only binary arrays (containing ones or zeroes) can be packed."
            )

        return out

    if arr.size == 0:
        return b""

    # Test array
    ds.PixelData = data if len(data) % 2 == 0 else b"".join((data, b"\x00"))
    elem = ds["PixelData"]
    elem.VR = VR.OB if ds.BitsAllocated <= 8 else VR.OW
    elem.is_undefined_length = False

    ds._pixel_array = None
    ds._pixel_id = {}

    if not tsyntax or tsyntax.is_compressed:
        ds.file_meta.TransferSyntaxUID = ExplicitVRLittleEndian

    # New pixel data always requires a new UID
    if generate_instance_uid:
        ds.SOPInstanceUID = ds.file_meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID = generate_uid()


def unpack_bits(src: bytes, as_array: bool = True) -> "np.ndarray | bytes":
    """Unpack the bit-packed data in `src`.

    Suitable for use when (0028,0011) *Bits Allocated* or (60xx,0100) *Overlay
    Bits Allocated* is 1.

    If `NumPy <https://numpy.org/>`_ is available then it will be used to
    unpack the data, otherwise only the standard library will be used, which
    is about 20 times slower.

    .. versionchanged:: 2.3

        Added the `as_array` keyword parameter, support for unpacking
        without NumPy, and added :class:`bytes` as a possible return type

    Parameters
    ----------
    src : bytes
        The bit-packed data.
    as_array : bool, optional
        If ``False`` then return the unpacked data as :class:`bytes`, otherwise
        return a :class:`numpy.ndarray` (default, requires NumPy).

    Returns
    -------
    bytes or numpy.ndarray
        The unpacked data as an :class:`numpy.ndarray` (if NumPy is available
        and ``as_array == True``) or :class:`bytes` otherwise.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `as_array` is ``True`` and NumPy is not available.

    References
    ----------
    DICOM Standard, Part 5,
    :dcm:`Section 8.1.1<part05/chapter_8.html#sect_8.1.1>` and
    :dcm:`Annex D<part05/chapter_D.html>`
    """
    if HAVE_NP:
        arr = np.frombuffer(src, dtype="u1")
        arr = np.unpackbits(arr, bitorder="little")

        return arr if as_array else arr.tobytes()

    if as_array:
        raise ValueError("unpack_bits() requires NumPy if 'as_array = True'")

    return b"".join(map(_UNPACK_LUT.__getitem__, src))

        cls = self.__class__

        # May be multi-valued, but let pydicom.charset handle all logic on that

        # Shortcut to the decode function in pydicom.charset
        decode_data_element = pydicom.charset.decode_element

        # Callback for walk(), to decode the chr strings if necessary
        # This simply calls the pydicom.charset.decode_element function
        def decode_callback(ds: "Dataset", data_element: DataElement) -> None:

            if data_element.VR == VR_.SQ:

        tag = cast(BaseTag, tag_for_keyword(name))
        if tag is not None and tag in self._dict:
            del self._dict[tag]

            # Deleting pixel data resets the stored array

class EncapsulatedBuffer(BufferedIOBase):
    """Convenience class for managing the encapsulation of one or more buffers
    containing compressed *Pixel Data*.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0
    """

    def __init__(self, buffers: list[BufferedIOBase], use_bot: bool = False) -> None:
        """Create a new class instance.

        Parameters
        ----------
        buffers : list[io.BufferedIOBase]
            The buffered pixel data frames to be encapsulated on writing the dataset.
            Only a single frame of pixel data can be in each buffer and the buffers
            must inherit from :class:`io.BufferedIODBase` and be readable and seekable.
        use_bot : bool, optional
            If ``True`` then the Basic Offset Table will include the offsets for
            each encapsulated items, otherwise no offsets will be included (default).
        """
        if not isinstance(buffers, list):
            raise TypeError(
                "'buffers' must be a list of objects that inherit from "
                "'io.BufferedIOBase'"
            )

        # The items to be encapsulated
        self._items = [_BufferedItem(b) for b in buffers]

        # The current position of the encapsulated buffer
        self._offset = 0

        # Use a non-empty Basic Offset Table
        self._use_bot = use_bot

        # The basic offset table
        bot = self.basic_offset_table

        # Offsets for the buffered items
        # Start of the item tag for the Basic Offset Table
        self._item_offsets = [0]
        # Start of the item tag for each frame
        self._item_offsets.extend([offset + len(bot) for offset in self.offsets])
        # End of the encapsulation
        self._item_offsets.append(self.encapsulated_length)

        # A dict containing the items to read encoded data from
        #   0: the buffered Basic Offset Table value
        #   1 to len(buffers): the buffered frames
        self._buffers = {idx + 1: item for idx, item in enumerate(self._items)}
        self._buffers[0] = _BufferedItem(BytesIO(bot[8:]))

    @property
    def basic_offset_table(self) -> bytes:
        """Return an encoded Basic Offset Table."""
        if not self._use_bot:
            return b"\xfe\xff\x00\xe0\x00\x00\x00\x00"

        # The item tag for the offset table
        bot = [b"\xfe\xff\x00\xe0"]
        # Add the item length
        bot.append(pack("<I", 4 * len(self.offsets)))
        # Add the item value
        bot.append(pack(f"<{len(self.offsets)}I", *self.offsets))

        return b"".join(bot)

    @property
    def closed(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if any of the encapsulated buffers are closed."""
        return any(item.buffer.closed for item in self._items)

    @property
    def extended_lengths(self) -> bytes:
        """Return an encoded *Extended Offset Table Lengths* value from `lengths`

        Returns
        -------
        bytes
            The encoded lengths of the frame.
        """
        # Exclude the item tag and item length
        return pack(f"<{len(self.lengths)}Q", *(length - 8 for length in self.lengths))

    @property
    def extended_offsets(self) -> bytes:
        """Return an encoded *Extended Offset Table* value from `offsets`

        Returns
        -------
        bytes
            The encoded offsets to the first byte of the item tag of the first fragment
            for every frame, as measured from the first byte of the first item tag
            following the empty Basic Offset Table Item.
        """
        return pack(f"<{len(self.offsets)}Q", *self.offsets)

    @property
    def encapsulated_length(self) -> int:
        """Return the total length of the encapulated *Pixel Data* value."""
        return len(self.basic_offset_table) + sum(self.lengths)

    @property
    def lengths(self) -> list[int]:
        """Return the encapsulated item lengths."""
        return [item.length for item in self._items]

    @property
    def offsets(self) -> list[int]:
        """Return the encapsulated item offsets, starting at 0 for the first item."""
        return [sum(self.lengths[0:idx]) for idx, _ in enumerate(self.lengths)]

    def read(self, size: int | None = 8192, /) -> bytes:
        """Read up to `size` bytes of data from the encapsulated buffers.

        Parameters
        ----------
        size : int, optional
            The amount of data to be read, if ``None`` then all data will be returned.

        Returns
        -------
        bytes
            The data read from the encapsulated buffers.
        """
        if self._offset >= self.encapsulated_length:
            return b""

        size = self.encapsulated_length if size is None else size

        nr_read = 0
        out = bytearray()
        while length := (size - nr_read):
            iterator = enumerate(zip(self._item_offsets, self._item_offsets[1:]))
            for idx, (start, end) in iterator:
                if start <= self._offset < end:
                    _read = self._buffers[idx].read(self._offset - start, length)
                    break

            if not _read:
                break

            self._offset += len(_read)
            nr_read += len(_read)
            out.extend(_read)

            if self._offset >= self.encapsulated_length:
                break

        return bytes(out)

    def readable(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if all the encapsulated buffers are readable."""
        return all(item.buffer.readable() for item in self._items)

    def seek(self, offset: int, whence: int = os.SEEK_SET, /) -> int:
        """Change the encapsulated buffers position to the given byte `offset`,
        relative to the position indicated by `whence` and return the new absolute
        position.
        """
        if whence not in (os.SEEK_SET, os.SEEK_CUR, os.SEEK_END):
            raise ValueError("Invalid 'whence' value, should be 0, 1 or 2")

        # Behavior emulates io.BytesIO
        if whence == os.SEEK_SET:
            # relative to beginning of buffer
            if offset < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"Negative seek 'offset' value {offset}")

            new_offset = offset
        elif whence == os.SEEK_CUR:
            # relative to current buffer position
            new_offset = self._offset + offset
            new_offset = 0 if new_offset < 0 else new_offset
        elif whence == os.SEEK_END:
            # relative to end of the buffer
            new_offset = self.encapsulated_length + offset
            new_offset = 0 if new_offset < 0 else new_offset

        self._offset = new_offset

        return self._offset

    def seekable(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if all the encapsulated buffers are seekable."""
        return all(item.buffer.seekable() for item in self._items)

    def tell(self) -> int:
        """Return the current stream position of the encapsulated buffers"""
        return self._offset

        if index >= len(basic_offsets):

                "There aren't enough offsets in the Basic Offset Table for "
                f"{index + 1} frames"
            )

        # There may be multiple fragments per frame
        if index < len(basic_offsets) - 1:

            length = basic_offsets[index + 1] - basic_offsets[index]

            fragments = generate_fragments(buffer.read(length), endianness=endianness)
        else:

            fragments = generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)

        buffer.seek(starting_position)

    # No basic or extended offset table
    # Determine the number of fragments in `buffer` an their offsets
    nr_fragments, fragment_offsets = parse_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)
    # `buffer` is positioned at the end of the basic offsets table

    # Single fragment must be 1 frame
    if nr_fragments == 1:

    #   multiple fragments and may be one or more frames
    if not number_of_frames:

            "pixel data as there is no basic or extended offset table data and "
            "the number of frames has not been supplied"
        )

    # 1 fragment per frame, for N frames
    if nr_fragments == number_of_frames:
        if index > nr_fragments - 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Found {nr_fragments} frame fragments in the encapsulated "
                f"pixel data, an 'index' of {index} is invalid"
            )

        # Covers RLE and others if 1:1 ratio
        # `fragment_offsets` is the absolute positions of each item tag
        buffer.seek(fragment_offsets[index], 0)
        frame = next(generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness))
        buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
        return frame

    fragments = generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)

    # Multiple fragments for 1 frame
    if number_of_frames == 1:
        if index == 0:

    #   last two bytes of a frame
    eoi_marker = b"\xff\xd9"
    frame_fragments = []
    frame_nr = 0
    for fragment in fragments:
        frame_fragments.append(fragment)
        if eoi_marker in fragment[-10:]:
            if frame_nr == index:
                frame = b"".join(frame_fragments)
                buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
                return frame

            frame_nr += 1
            frame_fragments = []

    if frame_fragments and index == frame_nr:
        warn_and_log(

            "JPEG EOI/EOC marker was found, the returned frame data may be "
            "invalid"

        buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
        return frame

    raise ValueError(f"There is insufficient pixel data to contain {index + 1} frames")

class _BufferedItem:
    """Convenience class for a buffered encapsulation item.

    Attributes
    ----------
    buffer : io.BufferedIOBase
        The buffer containing data to be encapsulated.
    length : int
        The total length of the encapsulated item, including the item tag and
        value and any trailing padding required to bring the item data up to an
        even length.
    """

    def __init__(self, buffer: BufferedIOBase) -> None:
        """Create a new ``_BufferedItem`` instance.

        Parameters
        ----------
        buffer : io.BufferedIOBase
            The buffer containing data to be encapsulated, may be empty.
        """
        self.buffer = buffer
        # The non-padded length of the data in the buffer
        self._blen = buffer_length(buffer)

        if self._blen > 2**32 - 2:
            raise ValueError(
                "Buffers containing more than 4294967294 bytes are not supported"
            )

        # 8 bytes for the item tag and length
        self.length = 8 + self._blen + self._blen % 2
        # Whether or not the buffer needs trailing padding
        self._padding = bool(self._blen % 2)
        # The item tag and length
        self._item = b"".join(
            (
                b"\xfe\xff\x00\xe0",
                (self.length - 8).to_bytes(length=4, byteorder="little"),
            )
        )

    def read(self, start: int, size: int) -> bytes:
        """Return data from the encapsulated frame.

        Parameters
        ----------
        start : int
            The initial position in the encapsulated item where data should be read
            from, must be greater than or equal to 0, where ``0`` is the first byte
            of the item tag.
        size : int
            The number of bytes to read from the buffer.

        Returns
        -------
        bytes
            The data read from the buffer.
        """
        """Return the encapsulated item lengths."""
        return [item.length for item in self._items]

    @property
    def offsets(self) -> list[int]:
        """Return the encapsulated item offsets, starting at 0 for the first item."""
        return [sum(self.lengths[0:idx]) for idx, _ in enumerate(self.lengths)]

    def read(self, size: int | None = 8192, /) -> bytes:
        """Read up to `size` bytes of data from the encapsulated buffers.

        Parameters
        ----------
        size : int, optional
            The amount of data to be read, if ``None`` then all data will be returned.

        Returns
        -------
        bytes
            The data read from the encapsulated buffers.
        """
        if self._offset >= self.encapsulated_length:
            return b""

        size = self.encapsulated_length if size is None else size

        nr_read = 0
        out = bytearray()
        while length := (size - nr_read):
            iterator = enumerate(zip(self._item_offsets, self._item_offsets[1:]))
            for idx, (start, end) in iterator:
                if start <= self._offset < end:
                    _read = self._buffers[idx].read(self._offset - start, length)
                    break

            if not _read:
                break

            self._offset += len(_read)
            nr_read += len(_read)
            out.extend(_read)

            if self._offset >= self.encapsulated_length:
                break

        return bytes(out)

    def readable(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if all the encapsulated buffers are readable."""
        return all(item.buffer.readable() for item in self._items)

    def seek(self, offset: int, whence: int = os.SEEK_SET, /) -> int:
        """Change the encapsulated buffers position to the given byte `offset`,
        relative to the position indicated by `whence` and return the new absolute
        position.
        """
        if whence not in (os.SEEK_SET, os.SEEK_CUR, os.SEEK_END):
            raise ValueError("Invalid 'whence' value, should be 0, 1 or 2")

        # Behavior emulates io.BytesIO
        if whence == os.SEEK_SET:
            # relative to beginning of buffer
            if offset < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"Negative seek 'offset' value {offset}")

            new_offset = offset
        elif whence == os.SEEK_CUR:
            # relative to current buffer position
            new_offset = self._offset + offset
            new_offset = 0 if new_offset < 0 else new_offset
        elif whence == os.SEEK_END:
            # relative to end of the buffer
            new_offset = self.encapsulated_length + offset
            new_offset = 0 if new_offset < 0 else new_offset

        self._offset = new_offset

        return self._offset

    def seekable(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if all the encapsulated buffers are seekable."""
        return all(item.buffer.seekable() for item in self._items)

    def tell(self) -> int:
        """Return the current stream position of the encapsulated buffers"""
        return self._offset

from collections.abc import Generator, Iterator

def absorb_delimiter_item(
    fp: BinaryIO, is_little_endian: bool, delimiter: BaseTag
) -> None:
    """Read (and ignore) undefined length sequence or item terminators."""
    if is_little_endian:
        struct_format = "<HHL"
    else:
        struct_format = ">HHL"
    group, elem, length = unpack(struct_format, fp.read(8))
    tag = TupleTag((group, elem))
    if tag != delimiter:
        logger.warning(
            "Did not find expected delimiter "
            f"'{dictionary_description(delimiter)}', instead found "
            f"{tag} at file position 0x{fp.tell() - 8:X}"
        )
        fp.seek(fp.tell() - 8)
        return

    logger.debug(
        "%04x: Found Delimiter '%s'", fp.tell() - 8, dictionary_description(delimiter)
    )

    if length == 0:
        logger.debug("%04x: Read 0 bytes after delimiter", fp.tell() - 4)
    else:
        logger.debug(
            "%04x: Expected 0x00000000 after delimiter, found 0x%x",
            fp.tell() - 4,
            length,
        )


def find_bytes(
    fp: BinaryIO, bytes_to_find: bytes, read_size: int = 128, rewind: bool = True
) -> int | None:
    """Read in the file until a specific byte sequence found.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fp : file-like
        The file-like to search.
    bytes_to_find : bytes
        Contains the bytes to find. Must be in correct endian order already.
    read_size : int
        Number of bytes to read at a time.
    rewind : bool
        Flag to rewind file reading position.

    Returns
    -------
    found_at : int or None
        Position where byte sequence was found, else ``None``.
    """

    data_start = fp.tell()
    search_rewind = len(bytes_to_find) - 1

    found = False
    eof = False
    while not found:
        chunk_start = fp.tell()
        bytes_read = fp.read(read_size)
        if len(bytes_read) < read_size:
            # try again - if still don't get required amount,
            # this is the last block
            new_bytes = fp.read(read_size - len(bytes_read))
            bytes_read += new_bytes
            if len(bytes_read) < read_size:
                eof = True  # but will still check whatever we did get
        index = bytes_read.find(bytes_to_find)
        if index != -1:
            found = True
        elif eof:
            if rewind:
                fp.seek(data_start)
            return None
        else:
            # rewind a bit in case delimiter crossed read_size boundary
            fp.seek(fp.tell() - search_rewind)
    # if get here then have found the byte string
    found_at = chunk_start + index
    if rewind:
        fp.seek(data_start)
    else:
        fp.seek(found_at + len(bytes_to_find))

    return found_at


def read_undefined_length_value(
    fp: BinaryIO,
    is_little_endian: bool,
    delimiter_tag: BaseTag,
    defer_size: int | float | None = None,
    read_size: int = 1024 * 8,
) -> bytes | None:
    """Read until `delimiter_tag` and return the value up to that point.

    On completion, the file will be set to the first byte after the delimiter
    and its following four zero bytes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fp : file-like
        The file-like to read.
    is_little_endian : bool
        ``True`` if file transfer syntax is little endian, else ``False``.
    delimiter_tag : BaseTag
        Tag used as end marker for reading
    defer_size : int or None, optional
        Size to avoid loading large elements in memory. See
        :func:`~pydicom.filereader.dcmread` for more parameter info.
    read_size : int, optional
        Number of bytes to read at one time.

    Returns
    -------
    delimiter : bytes or None
        The file delimiter.

    Raises
    ------
    EOFError
        If EOF is reached before delimiter found.
    """
    data_start = fp.tell()
    defer_size = size_in_bytes(defer_size)

    delimiter: BaseTag,
    is_little_endian: bool,
    read_size: int = 128,
    rewind: bool = True,
) -> int | None:
    """Return file position where 4-byte delimiter is located.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delimiter : int
        The delimiter to search for.
    is_little_endian : bool
        ``True`` if little endian, ``False`` otherwise.
    read_size : int
        See :func:`find_bytes` for parameter info.
    rewind : bool
        Flag to rewind to initial position after searching.

    Returns
    -------
    int or None
        Returns ``None`` if end of file is reached without finding the
        delimiter, otherwise the byte offset to the delimiter.
    """
    struct_format = "<H"
    if not is_little_endian:
        struct_format = ">H"
    delimiter = Tag(delimiter)
    bytes_to_find = pack(struct_format, delimiter.group) + pack(
        struct_format, delimiter.elem
    )

    return find_bytes(fp, bytes_to_find, read_size=read_size, rewind=rewind)


def length_of_undefined_length(
    fp: BinaryIO,
    delimiter: BaseTag,
    is_little_endian: bool,
    read_size: int = 128,
    rewind: bool = True,
) -> int | None:
    """Search through the file to find the delimiter and return the length
    of the data element.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fp : file-like
        The file-like to read.
    delimiter :
        See :func:`find_delimiter` for parameter info.
    is_little_endian : bool
        ``True`` if little endian, ``False`` otherwise.
    read_size : int
        See :func:`find_bytes` for parameter info.
    rewind : bool
        Flag to rewind to initial position after searching.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Byte offset to the delimiter.

    Notes
    -----
    Note the data element that the delimiter starts is not read here,
    the calling routine must handle that. Delimiter must be 4 bytes long.
    """
    data_start = fp.tell()
    delimiter_pos = find_delimiter(fp, delimiter, is_little_endian, rewind=rewind)
    if delimiter_pos is not None:
        return delimiter_pos - data_start

    return None

        """Append an item."""
        self._list.append(self._validate(item))

        """Remove the item(s) at `index`."""
        del self._list[index]

    def extend(self, val: Iterable[T]) -> None:
        """Extend using an iterable containing the same types of item."""
        if not hasattr(val, "__iter__"):
            raise TypeError("An iterable is required")

        self._list.extend([self._validate(item) for item in val])

    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `other` is equal to self."""
        return self._list == other

    @overload
    def __getitem__(self, index: int) -> T:
        pass  # pragma: no cover

    @overload
    def __getitem__(self, index: slice) -> MutableSequence[T]:
        pass  # pragma: no cover

        """Return item(s) from self."""
        return self._list[index]

        """Implement += [T, ...]."""
        if not hasattr(other, "__iter__"):
            raise TypeError("An iterable is required")

        self._list += [self._validate(item) for item in other]
        return self

    def insert(self, position: int, item: T) -> None:
        """Insert an `item` at `position`."""
        self._list.insert(position, self._validate(item))

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        """Yield items."""
        yield from self._list

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of contained items."""
        return len(self._list)

    def __ne__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `other` is not equal to self."""
        return self._list != other

    @overload
    def __setitem__(self, idx: int, val: T) -> None:
        pass  # pragma: no cover

    def __setitem__(self, idx: slice, val: Iterable[T]) -> None:
        pass  # pragma: no cover

    def __setitem__(self, index: slice | int, val: Iterable[T] | T) -> None:
        """Add item(s) at `index`."""
        if isinstance(index, slice):

        raise NotImplementedError(
